blocks.title: 📊 EST II Math Level 1 — Exam Blueprint & Domain Weighting
blocks.note: Official curriculum weighting and examination domain distribution for EST II Math Level 1.

body.en: The EST II Mathematics subject test is a rigorous examination for students in international and American-diploma programmes who wish to demonstrate advanced mathematical competency for university admissions. It covers algebra, geometry, trigonometry, and data analysis at a depth beyond the core EST I test.

label.en: ● Deep Conceptual Intuition — Test format & strategy

body.en: Proportional Invariance, Linear Structure & Quantitative Modeling: Across Egyptian Scholastic Test (EST II — Math Level 1), multi-step problems reduce to identifying invariant quantities—constant rates of change \(m = \dfrac{\Delta y}{\Delta x}\), conservation of total work/mass, or linear system rank conditions. A two-variable linear system \(a_1 x + b_1 y = c_1\), \(a_2 x + b_2 y = c_2\) has a unique intersection if \(\dfrac{a_1}{a_2} \ne \dfrac{b_1}{b_2}\), no solution (parallel lines) if \(\dfrac{a_1}{a_2} = \dfrac{b_1}{b_2} \ne \dfrac{c_1}{c_2}\), and infinitely many solutions if all three ratios coincide.

body.en: EST II Math is taken as a standalone subject test on the EST II examination day. It contains both multiple-choice and short constructed-response questions. The content aligns closely with pre-calculus and advanced secondary mathematics.

label.en: ⏱ EST II Math Level 1 Pacing & Calculator Strategy

body.en:
• Pacing Baseline: 50 questions in 60 minutes = 72 seconds per question. There is zero negative marking — never leave any question blank.
  • Three-Pass Execution: Pass 1 (Qs 1–25, ~20 min): bank routine algebra, basic trigonometry, and straight arithmetic. Pass 2 (Qs 26–45, ~25 min): solve conic equations, solid geometry, and multi-step probability. Pass 3 (Qs 46–50 & review, ~15 min): tackle non-routine proofs, vectors, and ensure all grid-in/bubble items are complete.
  • Calculator Mastery: An approved scientific or graphing calculator is permitted throughout. Use it to verify complex number computations, evaluate trigonometric functions in proper degree/radian modes, and solve quadratic systems.

label.en: ▲ The 4 Core Commandments for Scoring 750+ on EST II Math

body.en:
• 1. Never Leave Unanswered Items: With no penalty for incorrect answers, eliminate obvious extremes and make an educated guess whenever stumped.
  • 2. Verify Calculator Angle Mode: Trig questions in EST II frequently switch between radian measure (e.g., \(5\pi/6\)) and degree measure (e.g., \(150°\)). Confirm angle mode before performing numerical evaluations.
  • 3. Conic Identification by Inspection: Check the coefficients of \(x^2\) and \(y^2\): equal signs and equal coefficients indicate a circle; equal signs but different coefficients indicate an ellipse; opposite signs indicate a hyperbola.
  • 4. Memorize 3D Solid & Circle Relations: Sphere volume \(\frac{4}{3}\pi r^3\) and surface area \(4\pi r^2\); cone volume \(\frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h\); inscribed circle angle \(=\frac{1}{2}\text{central}\); cyclic quadrilateral opposite angles sum to \(180°\).

caption.en: EST II Mathematics domain distribution. Advanced Algebra (20%) and Functions (20%) together form 40% of the exam, complemented by Trigonometry (15%), Sequences & Complex Numbers (10%), Geometry (10%), Circles & Coordinate Geometry (10%), Statistics (10%), and Solid Geometry (5%).

label.en: ◆ Why It Works — First-Principles Derivation (Test format & strategy)

body.en:
Why Successive Multipliers & Harmonic Average Speed Work: If a quantity \(Q_0\) undergoes a percentage change \(p\%\) followed by \(q\%\), the compound multiplier is the product of individual scale factors:

\[ Q_{\text{final}} = Q_0\left(1 + \frac{p}{100}\right)\!\left(1 + \frac{q}{100}\right) = Q_0\left(1 + \frac{p + q}{100} + \frac{pq}{10000}\right) \]

Notice the cross term \(\dfrac{pq}{10000}\): an increase of \(p\%\) followed by a decrease of \(p\%\) yields \(Q_0\bigl(1 - (p/100)^2\bigr) < Q_0\). Similarly, traveling equal distance \(d\) at speeds \(v_1\) and \(v_2\) takes total time \(T = \frac{d}{v_1} + \frac{d}{v_2}\), so average speed is the harmonic mean \(v_{\text{avg}} = \dfrac{2d}{d/v_1 + d/v_2} = \dfrac{2v_1 v_2}{v_1 + v_2}\).

label.en: Worked Example A — Test format & strategy (Medium Application)

body.en:
Problem (Medium): In a right-angled triangle ABC, angle B is \( 90^{\circ} \). If \( AB = 5 \) and \( BC = 12 \), what is the length of the hypotenuse AC?

Step-by-Step Solution: This problem involves finding the hypotenuse of a right-angled triangle given the lengths of the other two sides. We can use the Pythagorean theorem, which states that in a right-angled triangle, the square of the hypotenuse (the side opposite the right angle) is equal to the sum of the squares of the other two sides. Let \( a \) and \( b \) be the lengths of the two shorter sides, and \( c \) be the length of the hypotenuse. The Pythagorean theorem is given by: \( a^2 + b^2 = c^2 \). In triangle ABC, we have: \( AB = a = 5 \) \( BC = b = 12 \) \( AC = c \) (the hypotenuse we need to find) Applying the Pythagorean theorem: \( AC^2 = AB^2 + BC^2 \) \( AC^2 = 5^2 + 12^2 \) \( AC^2 = 25 + 144 \) \( AC^2 = 169 \) To find \( AC \), we take the square root of both sides: \( AC = \sqrt{169} \) \( AC = 13 \) Therefore, the length of the hypotenuse AC is 13.

label.en: Worked Example \(B\) — Test format & strategy (Medium Application)

body.en:
Problem (Medium): Consider the function \( g(x) = ax^2 + bx + c \). The graph of \( y = g(x) \) is a parabola that passes through the points \( (1, 5) \), \( (2, 12) \), and \( (3, 21) \). If the vertex of the parabola is at \( (h, k) \), what is the value of \( h \)?

Step-by-Step Solution: Let the quadratic function be \( g(x) = ax^2 + bx + c \). We are given three points that lie on the graph of \( y = g(x) \): 1. \( (1, 5) \) \(\Rightarrow\) \( a(1)^2 + b(1) + c = 5 \Rightarrow\) \( a + b + c = 5 \) (Equation 1) 2. \( (2, 12) \) \(\Rightarrow\) \( a(2)^2 + b(2) + c = 12 \Rightarrow\) \( 4a + 2b + c = 12 \) (Equation 2) 3. \( (3, 21) \) \(\Rightarrow\) \( a(3)^2 + b(3) + c = 21 \Rightarrow\) \( 9a + 3b + c = 21 \) (Equation 3) Subtract Equation 1 from Equation 2: \( (4a + 2b + c) - (a + b + c) = 12 - 5 \Rightarrow\) \( 3a + b = 7 \) (Equation 4) Subtract Equation 2 from Equation 3: \( (9a + 3b + c) - (4a + 2b + c) = 21 - 12 \Rightarrow\) \( 5a + b = 9 \) (Equation 5) Subtract Equation 4 from Equation 5: \( (5a + b) - (3a + b) = 9 - 7 \Rightarrow\) \( 2a = 2 \Rightarrow\) \( a = 1 \) Substitute \( a = 1 \) into Equation 4: \( 3(1) + b = 7 \Rightarrow\) \( 3 + b = 7 \Rightarrow\) \( b = 4 \) Substitute \( a = 1 \) and \( b = 4 \) into Equation 1: \( 1 + 4 + c = 5 \Rightarrow\) \( 5 + c = 5 \Rightarrow\) \( c = 0 \) So, the function is \( g(x) = x^2 + 4x \). The x-coordinate of the vertex of a parabola in the form \( g(x) = ax^2 + bx + c \) is given by \( h = -\frac{b}{2a} \). In this case, \( a = 1 \) and \( b = 4 \). Therefore, \( h = -\frac{4}{2(1)} = -\frac{4}{2} = -2 \).

label.en: Worked Example \(C\) — Test format & strategy (Easy Application)

body.en:
Problem (Easy): Consider the function \( g(x) = 2x + 3 \). What is the value of \( g(4) \)?

Step-by-Step Solution: To find the value of \( g(4) \), we substitute \( x = 4 \) into the function \( g(x) = 2x + 3 \). \\ \( g(4) = 2(4) + 3 \\ g(4) = 8 + 3 \\ g(4) = 11 \) Therefore, the value of \(g(4)\) is 11.

label.en: Worked Example \(D\) — Test format & strategy (Hard Application)

body.en:
Problem (Hard): \( P(A) = 0.4 \) and \( P(B|A) = 0.5 \). Find \( P(A \cap B) \).

Step-by-Step Solution: \( P(A\cap B) = P(B|A)\cdot P(A) = 0.5 \times 0.4 = 0.2 \).

question.en: An EST II Mathematics examination consists of 50 questions with an allocated testing time of 60 minutes. If a student completes the first 30 questions in 33 minutes, what is the maximum average time, in seconds, the student can spend on each of the remaining 20 questions?
question.ar: An EST II Mathematics examination consists of 50 questions with an allocated testing time of 60 minutes. إذا كان a student compليكنes the first 30 questions in 33 minutes, what is the maximum average time, in seconds, the student can spend on each of the remaining 20 questions?

solution.en:
Step 1: Compute total available time in seconds: \[ 60\text{ min} \times 60\text{ s/min} = 3600\text{ seconds}. \]

Step 2: Compute time spent on first 30 questions: \[ 33\text{ min} \times 60\text{ s/min} = 1980\text{ seconds}. \]

Step 3: Calculate remaining time: \[ 3600 - 1980 = 1620\text{ seconds}. \]

Step 4: Determine average time per remaining question: \[ \frac{1620\text{ seconds}}{20\text{ questions}} = 81\text{ seconds per question}. \]

question.en: On the EST II Math exam, Advanced Algebra and Functions together account for 40% of the questions. In a 50-question test, if a student targets an accuracy rate of 90% in these two high-yield domains, how many questions from these domains can the student afford to miss at most?
question.ar: On the EST II Math exam, Advanced Algebra and Functions together account for 40% of the questions. In a 50-question test, إذا كان a student targets an accuracy rate of 90% in these two high-yield domains, how many questions from these domains can the student afford to miss at most?

solution.en:
Step 1: Find total questions from Advanced Algebra and Functions: \[ 50 \times 0.40 = 20\text{ questions}. \]

Step 2: Calculate 90% accuracy target: \[ 20 \times 0.90 = 18\text{ questions correct}. \]

Step 3: Find maximum allowed missed questions: \[ 20 - 18 = 2\text{ questions}. \]

question.en: [Practice 3 · Hard] In the diagram, \( \triangle ABC \) is a right-angled triangle with the right angle at \( C \). The length of the hypotenuse \( AB \) is \( 26 \) units. Point \( D \) lies on \( AB \) such that \( CD \) is the altitude to the hypotenuse. If \( AD = 4 \) units and \( BD = x \) units, find the value of \( x \).
question.ar: [Practice 3 · Hard] In the diagram, \( \triangle ABC \) is a right-angled triangle with the right angle at \( C \). The length of the hypotenuse \( AB \) is \( 26 \) units. Point \( D \) lies on \( AB \) such that \( CD \) is the altitude to the hypotenuse. إذا كان \( AD = 4 \) units and \( BD = x \) units, أوجد قيمة \( x \).

hints.en: In a right-angled triangle, the altitude to the hypotenuse creates similar triangles. Specifically, \( \triangle ADC \sim \triangle CDB \sim \triangle ACB \).
hints.ar: In a right-angled triangle, the altitude to the hypotenuse creates similar triangles. Specإذا كانically, \( \triangle ADC \sim \triangle CDB \sim \triangle ACB \).

hints.en: We are given \( AB = 26 \) and \( AD = 4 \).
hints.ar: تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \( AB = 26 \) ، \( AD = 4 \) لتبسيط الخطوة.

hints.en: Use the resulting form to finish: \(x = \frac{572}{26}\).
hints.ar: تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \(x = \frac{572}{26}\) لتبسيط الخطوة.

solution.en:
In a right-angled triangle, the altitude to the hypotenuse creates similar triangles. Specifically, \( \triangle ADC \sim \triangle CDB \sim \triangle ACB \).

Using the property that the square of the altitude is equal to the product of the segments of the hypotenuse (geometric mean theorem), we have \( CD^2 = AD \times BD \).

Alternatively, we can use the similarity between \( \triangle ADC \) and \( \triangle CDB \): \( \frac{AD}{CD} = \frac{CD}{BD} \) which leads to \( CD^2 = AD \times BD \).

We also know that in a right-angled triangle, the square of one leg is equal to the product of the hypotenuse and the projection of that leg onto the hypotenuse.

For leg \( AC \): \( AC^2 = AD \times AB \).
For leg \( BC \): \( BC^2 = BD \times AB \).

We are given \( AB = 26 \) and \( AD = 4 \).
The length of the hypotenuse \( AB = AD + BD \).
So, \( 26 = 4 + x \), which means \( x = 22 \).

Alternatively, using the property \( BC^2 = BD \times AB \):
We can first find \( AC^2 = AD \times AB = 4 \times 26 = 104 \).
Then \( BC^2 = AB^2 - AC^2 = 26^2 - 104 = 676 - 104 = 572 \).
Now, \( BC^2 = BD \times AB \) gives \( 572 = x \times 26 \).
\( x = \frac{572}{26} = 22 \).

A common algebraic trap is to incorrectly apply the geometric mean theorem for the legs. For instance, some might assume \( AC = AD \) or \( BC = BD \), or try to relate \( AD \) and \( BD \) directly using the lengths of the legs without considering the hypotenuse.

The value of \( x = BD = 22 \).

question.en: [Practice 5 · Medium] In the diagram below, lines AB and CD are parallel. Line EF is a transversal intersecting AB at G and CD at H. If the measure of angle AGH is \( (2x + 10)^{\circ} \) and the measure of angle GHD is \( (3x - 5)^{\circ} \), find the value of x.
question.ar: [Practice 5 · Medium] In the diagram below, lines AB and CD are parallel. Line EF is a transversal intersecting AB at G and CD at H. إذا كان the measure of angle AGH is \( (2x + 10)^{\circ} \) and the measure of angle GHD is \( (3x - 5)^{\circ} \), أوجد قيمة x.

hints.en: Since lines AB and CD are parallel and EF is a transversal, angle AGH and angle GHD are consecutive interior angles. Consecutive interior angles are supplementary, meaning their measures add up to \( 180^{\circ} \).
hints.ar: تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \( 180^{\circ} \) لتبسيط الخطوة.

hints.en: Therefore, we can set up the equation: \( (2x + 10)^{\circ} + (3x - 5)^{\circ} = 180^{\circ} \) Combine like terms: \( 5x + 5 = 180 \).
hints.ar: وبالتالي، we can set up the equation: \( (2x + 10)^{\circ} + (3x - 5)^{\circ} = 180^{\circ} \) اجمع الحدود المتشابهة: \( 5x + 5 = 180 \).

hints.en: Use the resulting form to finish: \(80^{\circ} + 100^{\circ} = 180^{\circ}\), which confirms our value of x.
hints.ar: تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \(80^{\circ} + 100^{\circ} = 180^{\circ}\) لتبسيط الخطوة.

solution.en:
Since lines AB and CD are parallel and EF is a transversal, angle AGH and angle GHD are consecutive interior angles. Consecutive interior angles are supplementary, meaning their measures add up to \( 180^{\circ} \).

Therefore, we can set up the equation:
\( (2x + 10)^{\circ} + (3x - 5)^{\circ} = 180^{\circ} \)

Combine like terms:
\( 5x + 5 = 180 \)

Subtract 5 from both sides:
\( 5x = 175 \)

Divide by 5:
\( x = \frac{175}{5} \)
\( x = 35 \)

Let's check the angles:
Angle AGH = \( 2(35) + 10 = 70 + 10 = 80^{\circ} \)
Angle GHD = \( 3(35) - 5 = 105 - 5 = 100^{\circ} \)

\( 80^{\circ} + 100^{\circ} = 180^{\circ} \), which confirms our value of x.

Common algebraic trap: Students might incorrectly assume the angles are equal (alternate interior or corresponding angles) or misapply the supplementary property. For example, setting \( 2x + 10 = 180 \) or \( 3x - 5 = 180 \).
